name: Sarmatism
summary: Sarmatism was the Baroque ideology of the Polish-Lithuanian nobility, who claimed descent from the ancient Sarmatians and saw themselves as an equal, free and martial ruling estate. It prized Golden Liberty (an elected, contract-bound king, a powerful Sejm, the liberum veto and a right of resistance), Catholic piety and ancestral custom, and it distrusted absolutism and foreign influence. It looked down on trade and held peasants as a lower, bound order.
scope: The Baroque noble ideology of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, c. 1575 to c. 1700 and its eighteenth-century decay: the origin myth of descent from the ancient Sarmatians confined to the szlachta, with the Golden Liberty political system, Catholic piety, patriarchal values and the antemurale christianitatis self-image that the defining sources (Frick, EBSCO, Filonik, Wilanów Palace Museum) attach to it. Excludes later Romantic nostalgia and the Enlightenment critics (Konarski, Bohomolec), whose views the sources present as reactions against it.
